title: Why Samajwadi Party never split? Akhilesh points out 'benefit' of dynastic politics
content: Akhilesh Yadav pointed to the presence of multiple members of his family in the SP and suggested that this had helped prevent a split in the party. "Have you ever wondered why the entire party did not split? Because there are five MPs from the same family. We also have several Muslim MPs, and some staunch socialists, so our numbers would not decrease," he said.

title: Mumbai hit-and-run: US national, 15, knocked down by speeding biker
content: A 15-year-old American student was injured in a Juhu hit-and-run incident. A speeding motorcyclist struck the teen while she crossed the road near Bhaidas Hall. She sustained a concussion, leg bruises, and a jaw injury from the collision. Police have registered a case and are actively searching for the fleeing motorcyclist. Activists noted the absence of speedbreakers due to Metro construction work.

title: 'Don't be desperate for wickets': Gautam Gambhir's message to Kuldeep Yadav
content: India returned to winning ways in the World Test Championship after a 165-run victory over Sri Lanka in the first Test at the Galle International Stadium on Wednesday. Four days after that win, the visitors will be back in action in Colombo for the second and final Test. India will be pleased with most aspects of their performance in Galle, but Kuldeep's form remains one of the major talking points.

title: Revanth Reddy not first CM to be denied MEA nod for foreign visit
content: Several opposition chief ministers and ministers have faced foreign travel clearance denials.  Telangana CM Revanth Reddy's recent rejection is not an isolated incident.  Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann and West Bengal CM Mamata Banerjee also experienced similar rejections.  Delhi CM Arvind Kejriwal and Kerala CM Pinarayi Vijayan were also denied foreign trip approvals.  These rejections highlight the MEA's role in granting political clearance for official visits.

title: Zohran Mamdani’s office skips City Council meeting on ‘second home tax’

The release of property valuations raised concerns about privacy and clarity among residents. In response, council members are actively pursuing answers and have prepared a list of inquiries for the administration.

title: Big crisis brewing in Rawalpindi? Pakistan deploys army for ‘sensitive duties’
content: The notification said the deployment was intended to prevent a potential security problem and ensure that authorities could respond quickly if an unexpected situation arose. It said that the decision was taken "to avoid any undesirable situation as well as to respond effectively in any unforeseen situation as per the requirement of the district administration".

title: 'Death only solution now': Teen replied to iPhone offer before jumping off hill
content: A teenager jumped from a cliff after his parents refused him a mobile phone. His father attempted to rescue him, and both fell to their deaths. The rescue operation turned into a tragedy as the teenager remained determined. Fire brigade teams deployed safety nets, but efforts were complicated by his movements. Police are investigating the exact sequence of events leading to the deaths.

title: SIM Card rules changing: What you can do and cannot do after August 24
content: New SIM card regulations will take effect from August twenty-fourth. Telecom operators must identify and inform customers exceeding their mobile connection limits. Initially, verification will occur post-activation, with a move to real-time checks by November. Subscribers in most of India can hold nine connections, while others have six. This system aims to prevent individuals from obtaining connections beyond the prescribed limit.

title: Railway fan spent 25 years restoring royal station, now on sale for £1.25m
content: Wolferton Station, a former royal terminus renowned for its regal service, has been reinvented as a charming family home. For over a hundred years, it welcomed members of the royal family during grand occasions. Following its closure, a dedicated railway employee intervened to prevent its demolition. Now, this unique property is available for purchase at £1.25 million.

title: Meta sued by former manager who claims he was fired over immigration letter
content: A former Meta manager filed a lawsuit alleging wrongful termination after objecting to an immigration letter. James Tillinghast claimed the letter overstated an employee's contributions and responsibilities. He also alleged Meta provided preferential immigration support to certain Chinese national employees. Tillinghast believes his dismissal was retaliation for raising these concerns. The lawsuit names Meta Platforms and a manager as defendants.

title: Fifth in WTC, two home whitewashes: Gambhir says India 'not struggling' in Tests
content: India go into the second Test against Sri Lanka in Colombo with a 1-0 lead after their 165-run win in Galle. But the series has also kept the focus on a team that is trying to build a new Test side after the departure of some of its biggest names.

title: NTA announces re-exam for 49 candidates after power failure at Jaipur centre
content: The National Testing Agency will conduct a re-examination for forty-nine candidates affected by a power failure. This re-exam for the All India Ayush Post Graduate Entrance Test is scheduled for September first. Affected candidates will receive revised admit cards with new examination centre details. The original AIAPGET 2026 examination was conducted on August twenty-second across India. This re-examination ensures affected students receive a fair opportunity to complete their test.

title: 'Will not step down': Manan Mishra reiterates as plea in SC seeks his removal
content: "I have served as the Chairman of the Bar Council of India for 12 to 14 years because I was elected. Manan Mishra represents 25 lakh lawyers; he will not step down simply," Mishra said. The lawyers demanding his resignation also sought the implementation of an Advocate Protection Act and questioned the proposed increase in registration fees at State Bar Councils.

title: How woman cop used power to force family into Rs 18 lakh land deal, suspended
content: Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Mohan Yadav ordered the immediate suspension of Katni CSP Neha Pachisia.  A case was registered against her for alleged coercion and fraud in land purchase.  The high court dismissed Pachisia's petition, denying her interim relief.  Investigators found financial irregularities and pressure on the land seller.  The police department has adopted a strict legal stance against the accused officers.

title: Raj Kapoor’s ‘Mera Naam Joker’ flopped in India, became a sensation in Russia
content: Mera Naam Joker achieved significant popularity in Russia after its 1972 release.  Hollywood dramas were banned, creating a void for Indian cinema.  Raj Kapoor was already a beloved figure due to earlier successful films.  The film resonated with audiences seeking dramatic and relatable entertainment.  This cinematic connection fostered a lasting cultural bridge between the nations.

title: When Sunita Ahuja opened up about her marriage to Govinda
content: In a reflective moment, Sunita Ahuja opened up about her enduring connection with Govinda, emphasizing both the struggles and the growth she experienced over the years. Despite facing emotional challenges, she discovered her own strength and identity. Ahuja acknowledged Govinda as her childhood love, hinting at themes of forgiveness, and described how their relationship blossomed into a frank friendship.

title: Deepika Padukone 'likes' post slamming Sandeep Reddy Vanga's brother

This situation has raised eyebrows about potential gender bias within the film industry. Fans have rallied behind Padukone on social media, while the role has now been taken over by Triptii Dimri for the project.

title: 'No compromise': BJP targets Congress over Vande Mataram decision; passes resolution
content: The BJP has condemned the Congress party's decision to sing only two stanzas of Vande Mataram. This move is seen by the BJP as undermining the national song's significance and legacy. The party passed a resolution to protect the honor and national character of the complete Vande Mataram. Union Home Minister Amit Shah also attacked the Congress Working Committee's resolution as anti-national.

title: 'My son took her to hospital': Jana Sena MP defends son after Aston Martin crash
content: MP Lingamaneni Ramesh stated his son is cooperating fully with the investigation.  The accident tragically claimed the life of a 26-year-old woman in Hyderabad.  His son immediately took the injured woman to the hospital after the incident.  Three medical tests conducted on his son have reportedly returned negative results.  The family expressed condolences and faith in the legal process to reveal facts.

title: Quote of the day by Susan Sarandon
content: Susan Sarandon, the esteemed actress, cherishes the process of getting older, viewing it as a valuable phase of life. She asserts that authentic beauty is derived from personal character and self-respect, rather than superficial looks. Challenging societal norms that highlight physical attractiveness, Sarandon promotes the idea of embracing aging as a natural and beautiful journey.

title: NBFCs stay on growth track as asset quality remains stable: Report
content: Non-banking financial companies anticipate steady growth ahead. Credit demand remains robust despite global geopolitical uncertainties. NBFC earnings showed strong growth in the first quarter of FY27. Vehicle financiers experienced accelerated asset under management growth. Gold financiers saw moderated growth and yield pressures.

title: India’s submarine hunting fleet gets stronger with indigenous warship Mangrol
content: The Indian Navy proudly welcomes Mangrol, its third indigenous Anti-Submarine Warfare Shallow Water Craft. This state-of-the-art vessel is crucial for enhancing coastal defense and forms part of an ambitious program to build eight such ships. With cutting-edge torpedoes and sonar systems for threat detection, Mangrol is primed for underwater surveillance and anti-submarine missions, bolstering India's capacity in shallow-water warfare.

title: 'Didn't back him': Gill questioned after Kuldeep bowled just 25 overs in Galle
content: Kuldeep bowled only 25 overs across India’s two innings in the Test and took one wicket, while left-arm spinner Manav Suthar and Ravindra Jadeja bowled around 44 overs each and shared 14 wickets. India won the Test by 165 runs.

title: ‘Sooryavanshi hasn’t played as much red-ball cricket’: Dravid’s blunt assessment
content: Rahul Dravid advocates for a well-balanced strategy for aspiring cricketer Vaibhav Sooryavanshi. He points out the crucial role of red-ball cricket alongside white-ball fixtures in a player's development. Such diverse training is anticipated to aid Sooryavanshi's growth. Dravid encourages patience as the youngster starts his professional path, reaffirming the sport's dedication to cultivating future Test cricket players.

title: 31-year-old Adobe techie beaten to death by wife’s family in Delhi

Police have detained four individuals in connection with the incident.  The engineer and his wife had been married for three and a half years.  An investigation is underway to determine the exact circumstances of the assault.

title: IndiGo A321neo grounded after tail impact during Gorakhpur landing
content: An IndiGo Airbus A321neo aircraft experienced a tail impact during its landing approach. The flight from Delhi to Gorakhpur made a successful landing on its third attempt. Scratches were observed around the APU inlet during a post-flight inspection. The aircraft remains grounded at Gorakhpur airport for necessary maintenance. Technical and regulatory clearances are awaited before the plane resumes operations.

title: Trade standoff: Trump's 50% tariff kicks in; Carney vows 'dollar-for-dollar' response
content: Trade negotiations between the United States and Canada fell apart after a three-day face-off. Canada called a halt to discussions, criticizing the US for presenting proposals that were both unfair and detrimental. In a dramatic move, the US introduced hefty tariffs on Canadian goods, prompting Canada to respond with an equal retaliatory measure. This failure to reach an agreement casts uncertainty over North American trade relations moving forward.

title: Tensions flare between ABVP, NSUI outside COEP hostel ahead of Rahul's Pune event
content: Tensions erupted between ABVP and NSUI members outside a Pune university hostel. Police detained several individuals following the Friday evening clash near the campus. A case was registered against NSUI and Youth Congress workers for alleged assault. This incident occurred before Rahul Gandhi's scheduled 'Chhatron ki Goonj' event. The event aims to discuss women's experiences and challenges in India.

title: 29 states vs Meta: How a landmark child safety trial could reshape Facebook, Insta
content: Twenty-nine US states are suing Meta, alleging exploitative product design targeting young users. The lawsuit claims Meta concealed internal research about potential harms to teenagers. States seek substantial financial penalties and court-ordered product redesigns for Facebook and Instagram. A former Meta engineer will testify as a key witness in the ongoing trial. This case could significantly influence future social media platform regulations globally.

title: ‘Say no to captaincy’: Ex-India cricketer’s big warning for Rishabh Pant

Former batsman Wasim Jaffer advises Pant to concentrate on regaining his batting form rather than taking on leadership duties just yet. Meanwhile, Axar Patel's captaincy is under the microscope following a lackluster season, with KL Rahul emerging as a possible alternative for the captaincy role.

title: Duleep Trophy: Sanat Sangwan, a Kohli & Lewis Hamilton fan, ready for next challenge

The 25-year-old amassed 828 runs at an average of 69, including three hundreds, and is gearing up for the next big challenge of his career in the upcoming Duleep Trophy, starting from Sunday at the BCCI's Centre of Excellence (CoE) in Bengaluru.

title: From border watch to deep strikes: Army raises first Baaz drone battalion
content: The Army has established its first dedicated drone battalion, the Baaz Battalion, along the western front. This new unit will operate under the Vajra Corps, overseeing sensitive border areas in northern Punjab. The Army is integrating more drones across various units for combat and support roles. Infantry battalions are receiving Ashni platoons, and artillery will induct Divyastra batteries.
